items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: She was back there with Mrs. Madam Willa Dobbs and them sisters, it was Rebecca Steel and all of them heavyweights.

ctx.x: Is that where you got your first organ experience? In the church?

Yes. Played a real church organ. Then we got a Hammond, but mother majored in music and church music you know. She was back there with Mrs. Madam Willa Dobbs and them sisters, it was Rebecca Steel and all of them heavyweights. And these average organ players, they don’t know what a [inaudible] is. They’re really not organ players. They’re not piano players either. They’re somebody with keyboard skills and they want to get the organ sound so they, you know, got a keyboard and learned how to play left hand bass.…

Yeah, I was just going to ask about left hand bass because that’s a passion of mine. And I was watching you on a video that someone did in their home. And you were really wailing on the B3 and you were doing the left hand bass. And it’s a powerful feeling because you can really control the music. You’re the bass player and the soloist, and the chordal person.
